questions.question: How do you say 'goodbye' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Adiós comes from 'a Dios' (to God) - like saying 'go with God' when you leave. Note the accent on the o.

questions.question: How do you say 'yellow' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Amarillo means yellow - picture a ripe yellow banana; the word also names the ají amarillo pepper.

questions.question: How do you say 'gray' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Gris means gray - it sounds like 'grease', which is often gray.

questions.question: How do you say 'bread' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Pan means bread - it is also the English word for a cooking pan, but in Spanish it is the bread on your table.

questions.question: How do you say 'cheese' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Queso means cheese - say 'KAY-so'; quesadillas are made with queso.

questions.question: How do you say 'book' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Libro means book - it looks like 'library', and a library is full of libros.

questions.question: How do you say 'chicken' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Pollo means chicken - 'pollo asado' is roast chicken, a common dish.

questions.question: What is the correct form of 'estar' for 'ellos'?
questions.explanation: Estar changes with the subject: ellos (they) takes están - the -n ending marks 'they', just like hablan.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Ellos goes with están.

questions.question: How do you say 'dog' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Perro means dog - roll the double r: 'PEH-rro'. A puppy is un perrito.

questions.question: How do you say 'fifty' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Cincuenta is fifty - it starts with 'cinc-' like cinco (five): five tens make fifty.

questions.question: What does 'Tengo doce años' mean?
questions.explanation: In Spanish, age is said with tener: tengo doce años means I am twelve.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Age uses tener in Spanish.

questions.question: How do you say 'good morning' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Buenos días means good morning - literally 'good days'. The accent falls on días.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Buenos días is good morning.

questions.question: How do you say 'white' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Blanco means white - 'blanco' gives us the English word 'blank'.

questions.question: How do you say 'black' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Negro means black - it is the root of the color word in many languages.

questions.question: How do you say 'milk' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Leche means milk - 'café con leche' is coffee with milk.

questions.question: How do you say 'Wednesday' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Miércoles is Wednesday - the accent on the first e tells you where to stress it: MEE-air-co-les.

questions.question: How do you say 'please' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Por favor means please - literally 'for favor'. Use it whenever you ask for something.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Por favor is please.

questions.question: How do you say 'February' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Febrero is February - it starts like the English word, but the b is soft, almost like a v.

questions.question: What is the correct form of 'ser' for 'yo'?
questions.explanation: Ser changes with the subject: yo (I) takes soy - the only form that starts with s-o-y, so it is easy to spot.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Yo goes with soy.

questions.question: What is the correct form of 'ser' for 'tú'?
questions.explanation: Ser changes with the subject: tú (you) takes eres - the -es ending is the clue for 'you'.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Tú goes with eres.

questions.question: How do you say 'mother' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Madre means mother - it looks like 'maternal'; 'mi madre' is my mother.

questions.question: What does 'Me gusta' mean?
questions.explanation: Me gusta means I like it (literally, it pleases me).
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Me gusta is I like it.

questions.question: How do you say 'Sunday' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Domingo is Sunday - it comes from the Latin word for the Lord's day, like 'dominion'.

questions.question: How do you say 'I am thirsty' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Thirst uses tener: tengo sed means I am thirsty.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Thirst uses tengo sed.

questions.question: What is the capital of Spain?
questions.explanation: Madrid is the capital of Spain - it sits in the center of the country, and the royal palace is there.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Madrid is Spain's capital.

questions.question: How do you say 'red' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Rojo means red - 'rojo' sounds a bit like 'rose', which is often red.

questions.question: What is the correct word order for 'the big dog' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Adjectives usually follow the noun: el perro grande.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: El perro grande is correct.

questions.question: How do you say 'one' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Uno is one - it is also the name of the card game, and 'un' is the short form before a masculine noun.

questions.question: How do you say 'I like soccer' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Me gusta is used with a singular thing: me gusta el fútbol.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Me gusta goes with one thing.

questions.question: How do you say 'ten' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Diez is ten - 'diez' sounds like 'de-ETH'; ten fingers are diez dedos.

questions.question: How do you conjugate 'hablar' for 'tú'?
questions.explanation: For -ar verbs, tú takes -as: hablas.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Tú -ar verbs end in -as.

questions.question: How do you conjugate 'hablar' for 'nosotros'?
questions.explanation: For -ar verbs, nosotros takes -amos: hablamos.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Nosotros -ar verbs end in -amos.

questions.question: What does '¿Cómo te llamas?' mean?
questions.explanation: ¿Cómo te llamas? asks 'What is your name?' - literally 'How do you call yourself?' The accent on cómo marks the question word.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: ¿Cómo te llamas? asks your name.

questions.question: How do you say 'six' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Seis is six - it sounds like 'says' with an s at the end: seis.

questions.question: How do you say 'uncle' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Tío means uncle - the accent on the i tells you to stress it: TEE-oh. Your aunt is tía.

questions.question: How do you say 'hello' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Hola means hello - the h is silent, so it sounds like 'OH-lah'.

questions.question: How do you say 'water' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Agua means water - 'agua' is also in 'aquarium', where water lives.

questions.question: How do you say 'twelve' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Doce is twelve - it starts with 'do-' like 'dos' (two): twelve is ten plus two.

questions.question: How do you say 'grandfather' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Abuelo means grandfather - 'abuelo' shares its root with 'abuelita' (grandma).

questions.question: How do you say 'seven' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Siete is seven - it sounds like 'see-ET-eh'; seven days are siete días.

questions.question: When do you use 'ser' instead of 'estar'?
questions.explanation: Ser is for lasting traits, while estar is for location, feelings, and temporary states.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Ser is for who you are; estar is for how you are.

questions.question: How do you answer '¿Cómo te llamas?'
questions.explanation: Me llamo means 'my name is' - literally 'I call myself'. Answer with 'Me llamo' plus your name.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Me llamo introduces your name.

questions.question: How do you say 'apple' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Manzana means apple - 'manzana' also means a city block in Spanish, but for fruit it is the apple.

questions.question: How do you say 'father' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Padre means father - it looks like 'paternal'; 'mi padre' is my father.

questions.question: Which sentence uses 'ser' correctly?
questions.explanation: Ser is used for origin: soy de Arizona means I am from Arizona.

questions.question: How do you say 'good afternoon' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Buenas tardes means good afternoon - use it from about noon until sunset; after dark switch to buenas noches.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Buenas tardes is good afternoon.

questions.question: How do you say 'aunt' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Tía means aunt - the accent on the i tells you to stress it: TEE-ah. Your uncle is tío.

questions.question: How do you say 'January' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Enero is January - the first month of the year; the j in English becomes a soft sound in Spanish.

questions.question: Which sentence uses 'estar' correctly?
questions.explanation: Estar is used for location: estoy en la escuela means I am at school.

questions.question: How do you say 'We study' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Estudiar is an -ar verb, and nosotros takes -amos: estudiamos.

questions.question: How do you say 'sister' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Hermana means sister - 'hermana' shares its root with 'hermano' (brother); change the -o to -a for a girl.

questions.question: How do you say 'orange' (the color) in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Anaranjado means orange (the color) - it comes from 'naranja' (the fruit): the color is named after the fruit.

questions.question: How do you make 'libro' plural in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Add -s to words ending in a vowel: libros.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Libro plus -s is libros.

questions.question: How do you say 'I am fine' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Estoy bien means 'I am fine' - estar is used because how you feel can change; 'bien' means well.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Estoy bien is I am fine.

questions.question: How do you say 'I like apples' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Me gustan is used with plural things: me gustan las manzanas.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Plural things use me gustan.

questions.question: How do you say 'eight' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Ocho is eight - it sounds like 'OH-cho'; a spider has ocho patas (eight legs).

questions.question: How do you say 'twenty' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Veinte is twenty - it sounds like 'BAYN-teh'; twenty is two tens.

questions.question: How do you say 'green' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Verde means green - 'verde' looks like 'verdant', the English word for green and leafy.

questions.question: How do you say 'pink' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Rosa means pink - it is also the word for a rose flower, which is often pink.

questions.question: How do you say 'cat' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Gato means cat - 'gato' sounds like 'GAH-toh'; a kitten is un gatito.

questions.question: What is the correct form of 'ser' for 'nosotros'?
questions.explanation: Ser changes with the subject: nosotros (we) takes somos - the -mos ending marks 'we', just like hablamos.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Nosotros goes with somos.

questions.question: How do you say 'rice' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Arroz means rice - 'arroz con pollo' is rice with chicken, a classic dish.

questions.question: How do you say 'cousin' (male) in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Primo means male cousin - change the -o to -a for a female cousin: prima.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Primo is a male cousin.

questions.question: How do you say 'Saturday' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Sábado is Saturday - the accent on the first a tells you where to stress it: SAH-bah-doh.

questions.question: What is the correct word order for 'the red house' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: In Spanish, adjectives usually come after the noun: la casa roja.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Adjectives come after nouns in Spanish.

questions.question: What is the correct form of 'estar' for 'ella'?
questions.explanation: Estar changes with the subject: ella (she) takes está - the accent marks the stress on the a.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Ella goes with está.

questions.question: How do you say 'Friday' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Viernes is Friday - it comes from Venus, like the English 'Friday' comes from a goddess too.

questions.question: How do you say 'two' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Dos is two - it sounds like 'dose'; two eyes are dos ojos.

questions.question: How do you say 'I am hungry' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Hunger uses tener: tengo hambre means I am hungry.

questions.question: How do you say 'Monday' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Lunes is Monday - it comes from the moon (luna), like 'Monday' comes from 'moon day'.

questions.question: How do you say 'March' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Marzo is March - it is named for Mars, the Roman god of war.

questions.question: How do you say 'pencil' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Lápiz means pencil - the accent on the a tells you to stress it: LAH-pees. The plural is lápices.

questions.question: How do you say 'four' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Cuatro is four - it sounds like 'KWAH-troh'; four wheels are cuatro ruedas.

questions.question: What is the correct form of 'estar' for 'yo'?
questions.explanation: Yo estoy means I am (location or feeling).
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Yo goes with estoy.

questions.question: What does '¿Cómo estás?' mean?
questions.explanation: ¿Cómo estás? asks 'How are you?' - answer with 'Estoy bien' (I am fine) or 'Estoy mal' (I am not well).
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: ¿Cómo estás? asks how you are.

questions.question: How do you make 'lápiz' plural in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Words ending in -z change to -ces: lápices.

questions.question: What is the correct form of 'ser' for 'él' or 'ella'?
questions.explanation: Ser changes with the subject: él and ella (he and she) take es - the shortest form of ser.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Él and ella go with es.

questions.question: How do you say 'thank you' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Gracias means thank you - it comes from the Latin word for grace; always pair it with 'por favor'.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Gracias is thank you.

questions.question: How do you say 'one hundred' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Cien is one hundred - use 'cien' for exactly 100; for 101 and up it becomes 'ciento'.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Cien is one hundred.

questions.question: How do you conjugate 'hablar' (to speak) for 'yo'?
questions.explanation: For -ar verbs, yo takes -o: hablo.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Yo -ar verbs end in -o.

questions.question: How do you conjugate 'hablar' for 'ellos'?
questions.explanation: For -ar verbs, ellos takes -an: hablan.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Ellos -ar verbs end in -an.

questions.question: How do you say 'eleven' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Once is eleven - careful: it looks like the English word 'once' but it means eleven, not one time.

questions.question: How do you say 'purple' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Morado means purple - it comes from 'mora' (blackberry), a purple fruit.

questions.question: How do you say 'Thursday' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Jueves is Thursday - it is named for Jupiter (Jove), the king of the Roman gods.

questions.question: What is the capital of Mexico?
questions.explanation: Mexico City is the capital of Mexico - it is one of the largest cities in the world, built where the Aztec capital stood.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Mexico City is Mexico's capital.

questions.question: How do you say 'three' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Tres is three - it sounds like 'trace'; three is 'tres' in Spanish and 'trois' in French.

questions.question: How do you say 'nine' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Nueve is nine - it sounds like 'NWAY-veh'; nine months are nueve meses.

questions.question: What is the correct form of 'estar' for 'tú'?
questions.explanation: Estar changes with the subject: tú (you) takes estás - the -as ending marks 'you', just like hablas.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Tú goes with estás.

questions.question: How do you say 'blue' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Azul means blue - 'azul' sounds like 'azure', the English word for sky blue.

questions.question: What is the correct form of 'ser' for 'ellos'?
questions.explanation: Ser changes with the subject: ellos (they) take son - the -n ending marks 'they', just like hablan.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Ellos goes with son.

questions.question: How do you say 'thirty' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Treinta is thirty - it starts with 'tre-' like 'tres' (three): three tens make thirty.

questions.question: How do you say 'house' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Casa means house - 'casa' is also in 'casita', a little house; 'en casa' means at home.

questions.question: How do you say 'grandmother' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Abuela means grandmother - 'abuela' shares its root with 'abuelo' (grandfather); change the -o to -a.

questions.question: How do you say 'Tuesday' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Martes is Tuesday - it is named for Mars, like March (marzo).

questions.question: How do you say 'brother' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Hermano means brother - 'hermano' shares its root with 'hermana' (sister); change the -a to -o for a boy.

questions.question: How do you say 'orange' (the fruit) in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Naranja means orange (the fruit) - the color anaranjado is named after this fruit.

questions.question: How do you say 'five' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Cinco is five - it sounds like 'SINK-oh'; five fingers are cinco dedos.

questions.question: How do you say 'school' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Escuela means school - it looks like 'school' with an e in front; 'la escuela' is the school.

questions.question: How do you say 'good night' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Buenas noches means good night - use it in the evening and when saying goodbye at night.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Buenas noches is good night.

questions.question: How do you say 'I speak Spanish' in Spanish?
questions.explanation: For -ar verbs, yo takes -o: hablo. The -o ending is the clue for 'I'.
